1.why: Server-side authorization is enforced on MFA endpoints by checking session.userId against USER.id in getSession.

2.why: Verification codes are single-use (session.identity!.used = true), but the same code could theoretically work for any user if session ownership is not properly validated (though in practice, session.userId is checked).

3.why: Previous sessions are not invalidated when MFA is enabled; only the new session is created (old session is deleted only if a new login occurs).

4.why: OTP shared secret is encrypted (AES-GCM) and backup codes are hashed (PBKDF2) before storage.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are not stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (session cookies are HttpOnly).

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed (e.g., regex checks for email, code formats, and length constraints).

8.why: Output encoding is applied in the frontend (esc function) to prevent XSS, and CSP headers further mitigate risks.

9.why: Redirects are restricted to an allow-list of internal paths via safePath function.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in the headers function.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are not exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (mock codes are only logged in TEST_MODE).

13.why: Verification codes are single-use (marked as used after verification) and time-bound (expires after IDENTITY_MS).

14.why: Repeated failed attempts are rate-limited (MAX_FAILURES) and locked out (LOCK_MS).

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on new login (token(32) generates a new ID), but idle/absolute timeouts are enforced, and logout invalidates the session. However, session rotation on authentication (e.g., after MFA setup) is not explicitly implemented.
